title: Anchor watch — debrief & runbook TODOs
content:
Anchor watch — debrief (2026-04-11)
Owner: Ramon Alvarez
Shift: 08:00–16:00 PT
Context: short handover from Priya at 07:50 — quiet morning then two noisy alerts around 09:12 and 12:37. This is my personal scratchpad; clean up into ticket(s) asap.

--- Morning checklist (quick) ---
- pulled latest escalation list (PD) and local contacts
- verified runbook links in Slack #sre-runbooks
- cursory look at dashboard: api-success ~99.97%, p50 latency 72ms, p95 540ms (higher than usual)
- rotated through pagerduty noise filter rules; left notifications unchanged but noted candidate alerts to tune

--- Active pages and immediate actions ---
1) 09:12 — RWD-2341: queue-backlog-increase (alert: queue-backlog > 1500 for 3m) — P2
   - Observed: spike in task-queue length for embeddings-worker-prod (eu-west & us-west).
   - Initial triage (09:14): Grafana top-plots showed concurrent CPU saturation on embedding pods in us-west-2; autoscaler did not trigger fast enough.
   - Quick mitigations: scaled embeddings horizontal pod autoscaler target from 6->12 replicas (kubectl scale hpa embeddings --replicas=12) at 09:20; manually increased GPU pool burst capacity (dedicated) via console at 09:22 to pick up pending pods.
   - Result: queue drained to baseline (~200) by 09:40.
   - Root-cause hypothesis: workload burst + delayed pod scheduling due to node provisioning cold-start in dedicated GPU pool; autoscaler vertical/horizontal mix not tuned for sudden concurrent bursts.
   - Notes: logs show transient scheduling failures: "insufficient nvidia-gpu" for ~2m window (09:16–09:18). Suggest provisioning buffer or warm pool.

2) 12:37 — 12:45 — api-request-timeout-surge (user-facing 504 spikes) — P3
   - Symptom: multiple 504s on text-gen single-replica routes (route: /v1/generate?model=small-llama) correlated with a single overloaded host running legacy variant.
   - Action taken: re-route traffic to canary pool via routing console (manual fallback) at 12:40; restarted the old host (kubectl rollout restart deployment/text-gen-legacy -n prod) at 12:42.
   - Result: error rate fell to baseline in ~6 minutes; p95 latency improved after restart.
   - Follow-up: need to mark legacy variant as deprecate candidate; it's producing AVL spikes with large multipoint inputs.

--- Commands / quick snippets used ---
- kubectl top pods -n prod | grep embeddings
- kubectl scale hpa embeddings --replicas=12
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="status=RUNNING AND labels:gpu"
- curl -sS "https://console.redwood/api/metrics?series=queue_length&env=prod&service=embeddings" | jq '.points[-1]'

--- Post-incident follow-ups (actionable) ---
- RWD-2341 follow-ups (assign: Priya) — due 2026-04-18:
  - Add warm-pool spec for embeddings dedicated pool (warm_nodes: min 2 always-on GPUs).
  - Update HPA to consider pending pod scheduling latency (custom metric: pending_time > 30s triggers earlier scale).
  - Add alert annotation for "insufficient nvidia-gpu" to auto-open infra ticket.

- Legacy text-gen variance (assign: Noah) — due 2026-04-15:
  - Create deprecate plan & migration checklist for legacy model variant; ensure traffic-shift + canary tests.
  - Add load test sim for multi-sequence long-inputs (to reproduce p95 spike).

- Runbook changes (assign: Ramon) — due 2026-04-13:
  - Update runbook: "queue-backlog" section to include explicit warm pool playbook and exact k8s commands used during this shift (copy exact kubectl/gcloud lines).
  - Add a short blurb on when to manually increase dedicated GPU burst capacity and link to billing/approval process.
  - Add checklist for "legacy variant restart" (include link to deployment health dashboard).

--- Runbook TODO (quick) ---
- [ ] Insert command snippet for scaling HPA with custom metrics (Ramon)
- [ ] Document warm-pool node label and minimum pool size (Priya)
- [ ] Create monitoring dashboard for "node provisioning latency" (Noah)
- [ ] Add test case in ci/load-tests for 300 concurrent embedding requests (eng-serving-runtime)

--- Notes to self / heuristics ---
- If queue-backlog alert hits, check 'kubectl get events' for scheduling failures (insufficient resources) before assuming code-level bottleneck.
- Warm pools are cheaper than repeated burst provisioning for frequently spiky inference workloads — propose budget estimate first.
- When restarting a host for latency spikes: prefer graceful rollout with canary traffic routing rather than killing host; kills can trigger cascading restarts for pinned jobs.
- Keep a 2hr follow-up window to confirm no regression after manual scaling.

--- Observability snippets (save to draft of runbook) ---
- Useful Grafana panels: embeddings/queue-length, node-provision-time, hpa-desired/current, pod-restart-count (last 24h)
- Quick Splunk query I used: index=prod "scheduling failure" OR "insufficient nvidia" | stats count by host | sort -count

--- Post-shift handoff (to Izzy at 16:00) ---
- Summary: two incidents, both mitigated. Main follow-ups in RWD-2341 + legacy-variant ticket. Runbook patches (short) should be merged before next week.
- Slack note drafted: @sre-team summary + links to RWD-2341 + PR #789; tag infra for warm pool cost estimate.

--- Loose questions / unresolved ---
- How common are bursts that require warm pool vs autoscaler tuning? (need historical query across last 30d)
- Can we automatically scale GPU warm pool without manual approval for up to N hours? (billing guardrails?)

--- Quick log (timestamps for handoff) ---
- 07:50 — handover from Priya
- 09:12 — queue-backlog alert (investigate)
- 09:20 — manual HPA scale triggered
- 09:22 — burst pool increased (console)
- 09:40 — queue baseline restored
- 12:37 — api 504 spike
- 12:40 — reroute to canary pool
- 12:42 — restart legacy host
- 12:48 — errors fall to baseline
- 15:30 — draft slack note + PR link added

End of scratchpad. Clean up and file the runbook PR + assign tickets before leaving.

Notes-to-self: when filing runbook PR, include exact kubectl/gcloud commands and a short test plan (how to validate in staging). Keep this doc until runbook PR is merged.
